I have a test on propositional and predicate logic for ΕΠΛ 111 (Διακριτές Δομές στην Πληροφορική, University of Cyprus). The lecture slides are in this vault as "1_-_propositional_logic.pdf" and "2_-_predicate_logic.pdf". Find them in the Logic folder and read both fully before writing anything. They are the source of truth: use their terminology, notation and examples. If anything in the slides seems wrong or conflicts with standard conventions, keep the slides' version and add a short "⚠️ Σημείωση" instead of silently changing it.

GOAL: Create exam-focused study notes in Greek.

LANGUAGE & NOTATION
- Write everything in Greek, using the exact Greek terms from the slides (e.g. πρόταση, σύζευξη, διάζευξη, αποκλειστική διάζευξη, συνεπαγωγή, συνεπαγωγή διπλής κατεύθυνσης, ταυτολογία, αντίφαση, συναρτησιακή πληρότητα, κατηγόρημα, πεδίο ορισμού, ποσοδείκτης, αντιπαράδειγμα, μάρτυρας, φωλιασμένοι ποσοδείκτες).
- The first time each term appears, add the English term in parentheses, as the slides do.
- Keep logic symbols as Unicode: ¬ ∧ ∨ ⊕ → ↔ ≡ ∀ ∃. Use T/F for truth values.
- Truth tables as Markdown tables.

STRUCTURE (create a folder "Λογική - ΕΠΛ 111"):
1. "00 - Ευρετήριο.md": index linking to all notes with [[wikilinks]].
2. "01 - Προτάσεις και Λογικοί Τελεστές.md": definition of πρόταση (with the slides' examples of what is/isn't one), all 6 operators, each with definition, truth table, a one-line "πότε είναι αληθής" rule and the slides' example. For → include: hypothesis/conclusion, why F→anything is T (the 100% → βαθμός 10 example), and all the ways to phrase it (αν P τότε Q, P ικανή συνθήκη για Q, P μόνο αν Q). For ↔ include its phrasings (ανν, αναγκαία και ικανή συνθήκη).
3. "02 - Προτεραιότητα και Μετάφραση.md": the precedence table (¬, ∧, ∨, ⊕, →, ↔) with the slides' bracketing examples, and translating Greek sentences into logic, including the τρενάκι example with both translations and the truth table showing they are equivalent.
4. "03 - Ισοδυναμίες.md": tautology, contradiction, logical equivalence (P ≡ Q iff P ↔ Q is a tautology). Method A (truth tables, and the 2^N rows drawback) with the five slide exercises. Method B: the full table of logical laws (identity, domination, idempotent, double negation, commutative, associative, distributive, De Morgan) plus the useful equivalences P→Q ≡ ¬P∨Q, P→Q ≡ ¬Q→¬P (contrapositive), P⊕Q, P↔Q. Include both worked proofs from the slides step by step, with the law named on each line.
5. "04 - Συναρτησιακή Πληρότητα.md": definition, how to build a formula from a truth table using only ¬, ∧, ∨ (the slides' S example, one conjunction per T row), and why {¬, ∧} and {¬, ∨} are also complete.
6. "05 - Κατηγορική Λογική και Ποσοδείκτες.md": why propositional logic isn't enough, predicates with one or more variables, binding variables (assigning values, quantifiers, or both, e.g. the P(x,y): x ≥ y examples), πεδίο ορισμού and why it matters (include the slides' ∀ and ∃ tables with answers), counterexample vs witness, the summary table of when ∀x P(x) / ∃x P(x) are true/false, and negation of quantifiers (¬∀x P(x) ≡ ∃x ¬P(x), ¬∃x P(x) ≡ ∀x ¬P(x)) with the Διακριτές Δομές student example.
7. "06 - Μετάφραση με Ποσοδείκτες.md": all the slides' translation examples, showing the step-by-step rewording the slides use. Clearly highlight the pattern: with domain "all people", ∀ goes with → and ∃ goes with ∧, and why swapping them is wrong.
8. "07 - Φωλιασμένοι Ποσοδείκτες.md": scope, nested quantifiers, expanding ∀x∃y P(x,y) over a finite domain {1,2,3}, the math-law examples, negating nested quantifiers (all four rules), order of quantifiers (when it matters and when not, with the x+y=0 and x+y=z examples), the harder translations ("ακριβώς ένας φίλος", the email/τηλέφωνο example, sum of positive integers), and the databases section (Codd, Flight/Airport queries, free variable determines the returned values, and why "is there a route with any number of stops" can't be expressed without a bound).
9. "08 - Τυπολόγιο.md": a one-page cheat sheet with every truth table, the precedence order, all equivalence laws, quantifier negation rules, and the ∀/→ vs ∃/∧ rule. Compact, for last-minute review.
10. "09 - Ασκήσεις.md": 15–20 new practice exercises in the style of the slides (truth tables, proving equivalences with laws, Greek → logic translation with and without nested quantifiers, negating quantified statements, evaluating quantified statements over a given domain, building a formula from a truth table). Put each solution in a collapsible Obsidian callout (> [!success]- Λύση) so I can test myself.

STYLE
- Each note: short intro line, then sections with headings. Use callouts for definitions (> [!note]), key rules (> [!important]) and common mistakes (> [!warning]).
- Add a "Συχνά Λάθη" section wherever relevant (e.g. F→Q is true, ⊕ vs ∨, "μόνο αν" direction, quantifier order, forgetting the domain).
- Link related notes to each other with [[wikilinks]].
- Be concise: these are revision notes, not a textbook. Don't add material that isn't in the slides, except the practice exercises.

When done, list the files you created and anything from the slides you were unsure about.

records.rawDisplayText: You don't need pdftoppm. Both PDFs have a text layer, so extract the text instead of rendering images. Install PyMuPDF with `pip install pymupdf` and extract the text page by page (fall back to `pip install pypdf` if that fails). Save the extracted text of each PDF to a temporary .txt file with page numbers marked, read it from there, and then continue with the original task. Delete the temporary files when you're done.
